faq.q: Do I need a boating license to rent a boat in Marbella?
faq.a: In Spain, you need a license to drive a boat over 5 meters or with an engine over 15hp. However, all our charters include a licensed skipper, so you don't need any license. You can relax while the skipper handles navigation.

faq.q: What boats can I rent without a license?

faq.q: How much does a no-license boat rental cost in Marbella?
faq.a: Prices vary. The Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39 cost €749 for 2 hours and €2,299 for 8 hours. The Mangusta 80 (white or grey) is €4,719 for a minimum of 4 hours, with a jet ski included. Other yachts are priced on request via WhatsApp.

faq.q: What is included in the charter price?

faq.q: Can I bring my own food and drinks?
faq.a: Yes, you're welcome to bring your own food and drinks. Many guests also request a catering service or a private chef—just let us know in advance. The included drinks and snacks are a bonus, not a restriction.

faq.q: How far in advance should I book?
faq.a: For peak summer months (June–September), book at least 2–3 weeks ahead, especially for weekends. For the Mangusta 80, which is popular, we recommend a month. Off-season, a few days' notice is usually fine.

faq.q: What happens if the weather is bad?
faq.a: Safety first. If the skipper deems conditions unsafe, we'll reschedule your charter or offer a full refund. We monitor forecasts closely and will contact you 24 hours before departure if there's a risk.

data.body_html:
Thinking about a Marbella boat rental no license 2025? You're in luck: in Spain, you don't need a license if you charter with a skipper—and every boat in our fleet comes with one. This guide covers the legal basics, costs, and the best boats for a stress-free day on the Mediterranean.

Why a Skipper-Led Charter is the Easiest Option

Driving a boat in Spain requires a license unless the boat is under 5 meters or has an engine under 15hp. Most rental boats exceed that, so the practical workaround is to hire a licensed skipper. That's what we do on every charter. You get to relax, swim, and enjoy the coastline while our professional captain handles everything.

Our Fleet: Boats You Can Rent Without a License

All our boats depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella's iconic marina. Here's a quick look at what's available:

For a full list, visit our fleet overview. Prices for other boats (Azimut 58, Pershing 46, Lagoon 380, etc.) are available on request—just message us on WhatsApp.

What's Included in Every Charter

No hidden fees. Every rental includes:

  • Licensed skipper and fuel
  • Water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava
  • Light snacks
  • Insurance and safety equipment
  • Spanish IVA (21%)

You can bring your own food if you like. Many guests add a catered lunch or a chef—just ask when booking.

How Much Does It Cost? 2025 Price Guide

The most affordable no-license options are the Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39. For a half-day (4h), expect to pay around €1,200–€1,500 (based on the 2h/8h pricing structure). A full day (8h) is €2,299. If you want more space and speed, the Mangusta 80 is a standout at €4,719 for 4 hours, which includes a jet ski.

For larger groups (up to 12 pax), consider the Ferretti 94 or Canados 86—both are priced on request. We'll give you a transparent quote within minutes via WhatsApp.

Where Can You Go? Top Routes from Puerto Banús

Your skipper will suggest a route based on the weather and your preferences. Popular options include:

  • Marbella coastline: Cruise past the Golden Mile, La Concha mountain, and the luxurious villas of Río Verde.
  • Cala del Faro: A hidden cove near Cabopino, perfect for swimming and snorkeling.
  • Estepona: A scenic 45-minute trip west, with charming old town views.
  • Sotogrande: For a longer day trip, head to this upscale marina and enjoy lunch ashore.

Most charters anchor for swimming and paddleboarding (available on request).

When Is the Best Time to Rent?

The season runs from April to October. July and August are the warmest (sea temps around 24–26°C) but also the busiest. May, June, and September offer pleasant weather with fewer crowds. Early morning departures (9am) give you glassy seas; sunset cruises (6pm–8pm) are magical.

How to Book Your No-License Charter

Booking is simple: choose your boat, send us a WhatsApp message, and we'll confirm availability. For the Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39, you can book directly on our site. For other boats, we'll send a tailored quote. A 30% deposit secures your date; the balance is due on the day.

Need help deciding? Read our blog for more tips, or contact us directly.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a boating license to rent a boat in Marbella?

In Spain, you need a license to drive a boat over 5 meters or with an engine over 15hp. However, all our charters include a licensed skipper, so you don't need any license. You can relax while the skipper handles navigation.

What boats can I rent without a license?

You can rent any boat in our fleet, from the 6.4m Mariah SX21 to the 29m Ferretti 94. Since a skipper is always included, there's no size restriction. For a private experience, consider the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39, both ideal for groups up to 11.

How much does a no-license boat rental cost in Marbella?

Prices vary. The Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39 cost €749 for 2 hours and €2,299 for 8 hours. The Mangusta 80 (white or grey) is €4,719 for a minimum of 4 hours, with a jet ski included. Other yachts are priced on request via WhatsApp.

What is included in the charter price?

Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). There are no hidden costs—just show up and enjoy.

Can I bring my own food and drinks?

Yes, you're welcome to bring your own food and drinks. Many guests also request a catering service or a private chef—just let us know in advance. The included drinks and snacks are a bonus, not a restriction.

How far in advance should I book?

For peak summer months (June–September), book at least 2–3 weeks ahead, especially for weekends. For the Mangusta 80, which is popular, we recommend a month. Off-season, a few days' notice is usually fine.

What happens if the weather is bad?

Safety first. If the skipper deems conditions unsafe, we'll reschedule your charter or offer a full refund. We monitor forecasts closely and will contact you 24 hours before departure if there's a risk.
